Image Credit: Enhanced Image by Gerald Eichstädt and Sean Doran (CC BY-NC-SA)/NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/MSSS

The dark surface bands are called belts, while the light ones are called zones. Belts are made of warmer gas that sinks into the planet, while zones are made of cooler gas that rises. At the intersection of belts and zones, you'll find massive storms, which look like spirals or ovals. (2/3)

🔭⚛️🧪🛰️

That's not an abstract painting, it's Jupiter's surface! As a gas giant planet, Jupiter has no solid surface. It's just one big atmosphere. This color-enhanced image from the Juno probe shows the turbulent and dynamic surface of Jupiter's bands and storms in vivid detail. (1/3)
